multimod

One optimization model, many representations.

multimod is an R toolkit for defining, translating, documenting, and solving algebraic optimization models. It stores a model as a common abstract syntax tree (AST), separating the mathematical structure from any one modeling language or solver interface.

From that shared representation, multimod can:

  • inspect, validate, visualize, fold, trim, and serialize a model;
  • render equations or a complete formulation as LaTeX;
  • generate GAMS, GMPL/MathProg, Julia/JuMP, Python/Pyomo, or R code; or
  • bypass generated model code and assemble a solver-ready LP matrix directly, write MPS, or solve in-process with HiGHS.

The package grew from energy-system modeling, but the AST and rendering machinery are domain-independent.

Why a common model representation?

Mathematical models often become coupled to the language in which they were first written. multimod separates three concerns:

  1. Model meaning — sets, parameters, variables, mappings, equations, and objectives in the AST.
  2. Representation — human-readable LaTeX, executable backend code, JSON, or a sparse LP/MPS matrix.
  3. Execution — a local solver, an institutional modeling environment, or remote hardware.

That separation makes it possible to compare backends, document the exact model being solved, manipulate it before execution, and reuse one formulation across several solver ecosystems.

Current capability

Direction Implemented
Define R constructors and DSL for declarations, references, expressions, and equations
Read GAMS models (partial language coverage); GMPL models and data (limited coverage)
Inspect and transform AST validation, model statistics, visualization, fold_model(), trim_model()
Document Equation and full-model LaTeX rendering
Generate code GAMS, GMPL/MathProg, JuMP, Pyomo, and plain R
Interchange and storage JSON AST serialization; Arrow IPC, Parquet, and CSV model workspaces with lazy data loading
Build matrices Sparse LP arrays, MPS output, coefficient diagnostics
Solve In-process HiGHS, written MPS, or generated backend code

Reader and writer coverage are intentionally reported separately. multimod can write languages that it cannot yet read, and parsing a source language does not imply support for every feature of that language.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

pak::pkg_install("optimal2050/multimod")

Backend runtimes are optional. Install only the solver or language toolchains needed for the routes you intend to use.

Quickstart

The package includes an energyRt-derived example model:

library(multimod)

mod <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
class(mod)
#> [1] "model"    "multimod"

eq <- mod$equations[["eqObjective"]]
print(eq)

Render the same equation in mathematical notation or executable languages:

as_latex(eq) |> cat()
as_gams(eq)  |> cat()
as_jump(eq)  |> cat()

Or inspect its expression tree:

as_visNetwork(eq)

To parse an existing source model instead:

mod <- read_gams("model.gms")
# or
mod <- read_gmpl("model.mod", data_file = "model.dat")

Document or translate a complete model

Produce a mathematical appendix directly from the model:

write_latex(
  mod,
  file = "model-equations.tex",
  title = "Model equations"
)

Generate code for another modeling environment:

save_model(mod, "model-workspace", format = "ipc")

write_gams(mod,  file = "model.gms")
write_gmpl(mod,  model_dir = "model-workspace")
write_jump(mod,  model_dir = "model-workspace")
write_pyomo(mod, model_dir = "model-workspace")

The generated code can then be executed with the corresponding local or remote runtime.

Skip code generation: build the LP directly

For a linear model, multimod can evaluate the AST into sparse solver arrays without asking GAMS, JuMP, Pyomo, or GMPL to rebuild the symbolic model:

lp <- model_to_lp(mod)
check_matrix_numbers(lp)

result <- solve_highs(mod, lp = lp)

# Or write a portable solver input:
write_mps(mod, "model.mps", lp = lp)

This route avoids the symbolic build step that can dominate time and memory on large models. solve_mps() provides the local file round trip; solution readers support HiGHS and cuOpt formats.

energyRt and cloud solving

energyRt uses multimod as a model compiler and interchange layer:

energyRt scenario
      |
      v
multimod AST --> LaTeX / backend code
      |
      v
   LP / MPS --> local solver
      |
      +------> mmcloud --> cloud CPU/GPU solver --> solution

With energyRt loaded, multimod::as_multimod(scen) builds the AST from an interpolated scenario. mmcloud can then transport an MPS file and solver command to cloud hardware and return the solution; multimod remains responsible for the mathematical model and matrix.

Development status

multimod is experimental. APIs and supported language subsets may change, and cross-backend output should be validated for the model features you use.

See the Get started article for the AST and DSL, the development status for backend coverage, and the roadmap for planned readers and transformations.
